messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: How to get RHadoop working in Rstudio
parts:
Rstudio doesn't pick up settings in your .bashrc file. You can set the necessary environment variables with Sys.setenv. See also a related discussion. I hope this helps


Antonio

On Tuesday, March 19, 2013 12:29:38 AM UTC-7, sLiang wrote:
I am brand new to RHadoop and I am used to IDE develop enviorment instead of console. I've tried hard to get RHadoop working on Rstudio + MapR on Ubuntu, e.g. using the instructions from RHadoop and MapR, check the LD_PATH, make sure the JAVA_HOME is in sunetc; but none of those worked. 

Here is some of the errors: 

> library(rhdfs)
Loading required package: rJava
Error : .onLoad failed in loadNamespace() for 'rhdfs', details:
  call: fun(libname, pkgname)
  error: Environment variable HADOOP_CMD must be set before loading package rhdfs
Error: package/namespace load failed for ‘rhdfs’

> library(rmr2)
Loading required package: Rcpp
Loading required package: RJSONIO
Loading required package: digest
Loading required package: functional
Loading required package: stringr
Loading required package: plyr
Error in library.dynam(lib, package, package.lib) : 
  shared object ‘rmr2.so’ not found
Error: package/namespace load failed for ‘rmr2’

However, I've using the below command before I use the library() function in .bashrc file for root:

export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-6-sun-1.6.0.26
export HADOOP_CMD=/opt/mapr/hadoop/hadoop-0.20.2/bin/hadoop
export HADOOP_CONF=/opt/mapr/hadoop/hadoop-0.20.2/conf
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/mapr/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export HADOOP_STREAMING=/opt/mapr/hadoop/hadoop-0.20.2/contrib/streaming/hadoop-0.20.2-dev-streaming.jar

Could anyone share how to get RHadoop working on it? Thanks a lot in advance.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#686] Re: How to get RHadoop working in Rstudio
parts:
Test with Sys.getenv() in the RStudio console, aka R prompt, to see if the relevant variables are set. If they are not, set them with Sys.setenv() and repeat your tests. I would worry about automating the procedure once we know which procedure we are trying to automate. Thanks


Antonio
